headline: Medium-risk shared MCP/filesystem interaction: ctx can observe Claude Code events while MemMachine exposes MCP and networked context handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while MemMachine exposes an MCP Server. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MemMachine content is fed into ctx or vice versa. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine outputs are routed into ctx-observed files or MCP messages
IF ctx treats observed tool output as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text
Restrict shared MCP channels to read-only payloads
Review one sample message flow for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add parser hardening and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content; MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context and can connect through MCP or REST. A shared workspace or MCP bridge could leak sensitive context between them. Because the exact deployment is undocumented, this is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server
IF either agent forwards file contents or conversation context to its backend
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Remove sensitive files from the shared directory
Turn off automatic context upload where possible
Check API logs for cross-agent payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, and MemMachine can use MCP with allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit shared write scopes, both can mutate shared external state through MCP-connected resources or browser-driven workflows. The overlap is plausible but not proven, so uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same MCP-backed resource
IF browser actions or package installs modify shared project state
mitigations: Assign separate target resources per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a lock file for shared mutable resources
Inspect recent writes before resuming
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative context by downstream automation. MemMachine consumes conversational context and can expose it through MCP or API, making it plausible that ctx-generated summaries flow into MemMachine without verification. The pathway exists, but no direct evidence shows automatic action-taking.
conditions: IF ctx summaries are ingested into MemMachine as trusted memory
IF downstream automation acts on MemMachine state without human review
mitigations: Mark ctx output as untrusted by default
Require a human check before memory writes
Compare summaries against source logs
Limit MemMachine writes to non-actionable notes
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and deletion policies if the same personal data class is shared. No residency or certification conflict is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same personal data is stored in both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Inventory which data classes each agent stores
Align retention settings for shared data
Delete stale logs and memories
Document deletion/export handling
requires-engineering: harmonize compliance controls across systems
